memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD." - Lev 10:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse is hard, and we should not soften it.

Notice the terrible symmetry. In chapter 9, fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed the offering, and the people shouted. Here the same fire, from the same presence, consumes two men.

The same holiness that blesses can also judge. God had not changed between the two chapters.

Many people today are comfortable with God's love and uncomfortable with His holiness, as though these were competing qualities and love had won. Scripture never presents them as rivals. God is love (1 Jn 4:16), and our God is a consuming fire (Heb 12:29). Both are true of the same God.

What do we do with a passage like this?

We hold it honestly. We do not explain it away, and we do not use it to frighten people into religion. We let it teach us that God is real, holy, and not to be managed — and then we look at the cross, where that same holiness fell on Christ instead of us.

Nadab and Abihu received what sin deserves. At Calvary, Jesus received what our sin deserved. The fire fell on Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I let God's love become sentimental in my thinking, detached from His holiness?
2. What does it mean that the judgement I deserved fell on Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are holy and I cannot approach You casually. Thank You that at the cross the fire fell on Your Son instead of me. Amen.
